description.narrative:
The outputs of the proposed Urban Project Preparatory Facility for Sri Lanka include (i) feasibility studies and detailed designs of urban projects completed; (ii) advance implementation support for two ensuing projects provided; and (iii) institutional capacity of implementing agencies strengthened. The outputs will result in the following outcome: high level of urban project readiness achieved. The project will be aligned with the following impact: urban projects in strategic cities and towns implemented in a timely manner. The TA loan will develop two projects listed in the country operations business plan (COBP), 2018-2020. Subproject selection criteria were prepared together with executing agencies, and projects to be developed under the UPPF were initially identified during fact-finding mission. Areas of value addition for ADB include piloting innovative approaches such as high-level technology to improve operational efficiency, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and address climate change impacts.
An attached transaction technical assistance (TA) of $1.0 million funded on a grant basis by ADB's Technical Assistance Special Fund (TASF-6) will provide capacity building and implementation support to the executing agencies in areas of procurement, technical appraisal, safeguards, disaster and climate change, governance improvement, strategic planning, financial management, revenue generation, and operational and maintenance capacity for improved service delivery.

description.narrative: High level of urban project readiness achieved

At least 30% of contracts ready for award before loan negotiations of ensuing project Progress/Status: ADB has decided to retain the loan closing date of 31 March 2024. This has been discussed and communicated to the officials in the meetings with the Department of National Planning and the Department of External Resources. The official communication dated 08 April was issued to ERD. A partial cancellation of $6.0 million of the undisbursed loan amount and reallocation of loan proceeds was processed and approved on 29 July 2024. ERD was informed via ADB letter dated 1 and 26 August 2024. Request to close the loan was approved and was effective on 9 October 2024.
For the Tourism SDP bidding documents for 30% contract (considering the loan amount) are ready for bidding. Data Source: Project performance reports Actual value:

At least 60% of detailed engineering designs completed before loan fact finding mission of ensuing projects Progress/Status: ADB has decided to retain the loan closing date of 31 March 2024. This has been discussed and communicated to the officials in the meetings with the Department of National Planning and the Department of External Resources. The official communication dated 08 April was issued to ERD. A partial cancellation of $6.0 million of the undisbursed loan amount and reallocation of loan proceeds was processed and approved on 29 July 2024. ERD was informed via ADB letter dated 1 and 26 August 2024. Request to close the loan was approved effective 9 October 2024.
Due to the recent economic crisis and change in government priorities, MUDH component was used to prepare a tourism and urban development project with $30m investment (reduced financing). 60% detailed design was completed of the project before the fact-finding mission. Data Source: Project performance reports Actual value:

Output: Advance implementation support for two ensuing projects provided Indicator: At least 30% of civil works bidding documents tendered before loan fact-finding mission for ensuing projects Progress/Status: 2a and 2b. Before the suspension of the project activities in August 2020:
- A standard bid document was drafted. Standard formats for estimates were prepared for preparing the bill of quantities of the bid documents.
- Environmental Assessment Review Framework was prepared for the ensuing projects.
- Preliminary safeguard assessment reports were prepared for 20 LAs under STSDP and 4 towns under SUDP.
The above draft documents were used to prepare the bidding documents for Tourism SDP. The strategic procurement plan (SPP) and the Initial procurement Plan was finalized. The safeguards documents for all the subprojects under Tourism SDP were prepared. Bidding is yet to commence.

This has been discussed and communicated to the officials in the meetings with the Department of National Planning and the Department of External Resources. The official communication dated 08 April was issued to ERD. A partial cancellation of $6.0 million of the undisbursed loan amount and reallocation of loan proceeds was processed and approved on 29 July 2024. ERD was informed via ADB letter dated 1 and 26 August 2024. Request to close the loan was approved effective 9 October 2024.

Output: Feasibility studies and detailed designs of urban subprojects completed Indicator: Urban subprojects prepared in at least 15 of 29 cities with climate- and disaster-resilient and gender-inclusive features Progress/Status: 1a. Before the suspension of the project activities in August 2020: - Feasibility studies for 20 out of 25 LAs under STSDP and all four towns (Dambulla, Trincomalee, Karunagella and Ratnapura) under SUDP were prepared with climate- and disaster-resilient and gender-inclusive features. - Traffic and Transportation plans for 3 towns were prepared.
The government planned to utilize these documents when investment projects in those LAs and Towns will be planned in the future.
For the investment component of the Tourism SDP, subprojects preparation in two towns (Trincomalee and Dambulla) was completed for the MUDH component. The attached TA 9590 was utilized to mobilize Individual consultants for the subprojects preparation.
Data Source: Project proposal reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity of project agencies strengthened Indicator: At least 100 officials (30% women) reporting increased knowledge or skills in procurement, contract management, safeguards, financial management, gender mainstreaming, climate change, and disaster risk management Progress/Status: 3a. Capacity building programs were conducted on procurement procedures and guidelines, and PPP covered around 80 participants including 30% women participants. MUDH developed a capacity building plan identifying the training to be conducted in 2023 targeting 30% women participation for all training programs.
Completed under the attached TA. Data Source: Post-training surveys Actual value:
